abstract: The measure of economic worth should be a development's net money flow, plus the value of all the options that it gives one to generate other money flows. These options are especially important in advanced manufacturing. Technologies and techniques that enhance the flexibility of a firm's manufacturing operations are an important source of options. And the fact that these technologies are applied in conditions of great uncertainty means that their successful exploitation needs such options. At present, the ability to use quantitative models to understand growth options is limited, and one has to rely on more informal lines of reasoning.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

There is an ever growing demand for prototype models in all sectors of industry, none more so than in the manufacture of cars, the insatiable demand for models of new components to support new vehicle development programmes is never ending. In more recent years the use of manual skills and artistic flair have played a major role in ensuring that these needs were fulfilled. Now models can be produced in a matter of hours instead of weeks or months using the rapidly growing rapid prototyping technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

Salford based ARRL has been involved with virtual reality and simulation for several years because of the potential value of these technologies to its mainline business with is robotics. ARRL has launched a major two year virtual reality and simulation initiative in collaboration with ten industrial companies. The purpose of this paper is to describe the initiative.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

The paper discusses automation techniques for the lay-up of nonrigid fabrics. A robotic cell has been established for the assembly of aircraft blade preforms from dry fabrics. The constituent components of the cell are briefly described and the system operational performances are outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modern applications of EDM and ECM
abstract: Presents some modern applications of both electro-discharge machining (EDM) and electro-chemical machining (ECM) processes. These applications are indicative of the wide spectrum of these processes and their ability to be adapted to help achieve difficult demands. Four applications are discussed. The first two applications employ the EDM process whereas the third and fourth applications utilise ECM principles. For each application the specific problem which needs to be addressed is presented, the proposed system to achieve these requirements is described and some typical practical results are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
